findings.text: The refusal covers exactly the five options its brief named, and the class is narrowed rather than closed. --models, --reviewer-profile (and its IMAS_CODEX_SN_REVIEW_PROFILE envvar), --batch-size, --neighborhood, -c/--cost-limit, --dry-run, --report-only, --skip-audit and --concurrency are all still accepted and discarded, because the groups branch returns at :6209 before any of them is read; I measured two of them (-c 1 and --report-only, both exit 0 with the worklist rendered). Two classes hide here and only one is defensible: -c/--cost-limit and --report-only are inert by construction on a target that spends nothing and writes nothing, which is presumably why the brief dropped them from the prior review's list, but a reviewer-selection option silently discarded is the same 'looks configured, is not' shape this node exists to repair, and a user passing --reviewer-profile opus-only to --target groups has no way to learn it did nothing. Either extend the guard to the reviewer-selection options or say in --target's help that the five scoping options are refused while the rest are inert.

`assert option in result.output` does not distinguish the guard's refusal from click's own parse error, so the case pins exit 2 and the absence of a rendered worklist but not the guard as the cause. Measured: invoking with `--bogus-option` also exits 2 and prints `Error: No such option: --bogus-option`, whose text contains the token; click's usage banner (`Usage: sn review [OPTIONS]`) contains no option names, so the banner is not the risk, but deleting an option from the decorator would leave this case green while the refusal it asserts disappeared. Asserting the guard's own phrase ("does not support scoping options") alongside the token costs one line and pins the cause.

The paragraph added to the module docstring does not parse: "so supplying one is refused rather than across a run that reports every family under a scoped-looking invocation" — the verb the sentence needs after "rather than" is missing, so the stated rule reads as a fragment. The previous sentence is fine; this one needs the lost word ("rather than discarded across a run ...").

justifications.durability: The delivered behaviour is real and survives re-measurement from two independent archives, and the refusal preserves the target's zero-cost property: my refused invocations ran with no graph stand-in installed and still exited 2 with the usage error, which shows the guard fires before build_worklist and therefore before any graph access, so the branch still reaches no model, spends nothing and writes nothing. Merging this node onto my HEAD is clean — `git merge-tree --write-tree 6fba57699 aab992ebb` returns a single tree with no conflicted stage entries, unlike the previous node whose plan-version line conflicted — and the figure parses as XML under minidom, which is what aab992ebb claims to have fixed. Two costs. The --stage leg of the guard is addressed by parameter name in a string (:5977), and click returns None for an unknown name, so the guard's refusal is only as durable as that string; the test catches the rename loudly (the run reverts to exit 0 against an assertion of 2), so this is a coupling to record rather than a live defect. And because the case asserts the option token rather than the guard's phrase, deleting an option from the decorator would leave the case green while the refusal it asserts disappeared.
justifications.evidence: The declared clause is met literally and I reproduced it from an archive of HEAD rather than from the worker's tree: `pytest tests/standard_names/test_grouped_review_target.py` gives 11 passed, exit 0. The remote control is genuine — the base revision reproduces the defect for all five options (exit 0, worklist rendered), which is the premise the repair rests on, and the worker's own evidence records the one trap in that reading honestly: `--physics-domain magnetics` exits 2 on the base because click's Choice rejects an unknown domain, not because anything refused it, and with a valid domain the option was discarded like the others — I confirmed the rejection text names the Choice, not the guard. The negative control is real and its red set is the right one: removing the guard call gives 8 failed, 3 passed, the eight being the refusal cases (six single-option including the supplied-default --stage, two multi-option) with the bare-run case still green, so the red is the missing guard rather than a broken command. Two deductions: the substring assertion cannot tell the guard's message from click's own unknown-option error (measured), and the recorded note enumerates its eight reds as 'the five per-option refusals, the two multi-option cases, and one duplicate param id' when the eighth is simply the second --stage case (the ids --stage-supplied2 and --stage-supplied3 are distinct).
justifications.fit: Naming and prose are by mechanism throughout: _refuse_grouped_review_scoping, ids/domain/unreviewed/force read by value and stage_filter by parameter source, no plan, sprint or ticket identifiers in symbols, filenames or comments, and no AI attribution. Both commit subjects are conventional and both carry bodies that state why, including why the parameter source is the only reading that distinguishes a supplied --stage from its default. The landing record is unusually well-shaped for this project's evidence discipline: it carries a before/after exit-code table, the declared mutation verbatim with its measured 8-of-11 red, and an explicit 'What the measure does not establish' paragraph that hands the live-graph compatibility to the merged-result test node. The figure is a flow whose primary content is sequential — where the guard sits on the branch and what each side produces — so a figure is the right form, though its lower blocks restate the exit-code table that sits directly beneath it. Deducted for the garbled docstring sentence, which is in a paragraph this node added.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The goal — the grouped target refuses a supplied option it cannot honour instead of accepting and discarding it — is delivered for the set the brief named and I verified both directions independently. From an archive of the base revision 6f9a29f9f, all five options were accepted: --ids equilibrium, --physics-domain equilibrium, --stage accepted, --stage drafted, --unreviewed and --force each exited 0 with the worklist rendered and no refusal in the output. From an archive of HEAD aab992ebb, each exits 2 with `Error: --target groups reports every sibling family and does not support scoping options: <the options supplied>`, an invocation carrying two names both (`--unreviewed, --force`), and the bare command still exits 0. The supplied-default case is the sharp one and it is handled: --stage declares default="drafted" (:6043), so the guard reads the click parameter source rather than the value (:5977), and I measured --stage drafted refused while the unsupplied default leaves the run at 0. Below full because the class is narrowed rather than closed: -c/--cost-limit and --report-only — both named in the prior review's finding — are still accepted and discarded, as are the reviewer-selection options, and neither the guard's docstring nor the landing record says the five are a chosen subset rather than the whole class.
justifications.scope_discipline: Three commits touch exactly the five fenced paths and nothing else: 47f5c0441 (sn.py, the test file), 1407f191c (the evidence archive, the figure, the plan), aab992ebb (the figure again, to fix an XML comment). The plan-version meta line is 36 at the base and 36 at HEAD — untouched, as the dispatch requires, so nothing was added to the merge conflict there. No followup was resolved: f-scai-groups-wiring and f-scai-getattr-aperture are both still open in the landed plan, and the node wrote its landing record as a paragraph in the section that carried the target rather than closing anything. The guard has exactly two occurrences in sn.py (its definition at :5951 and the single call inside the groups branch at :6201), so no other target and no other command can reach it — a structural fact that is stronger than the adjacent cohort run the manifest reports. The figure lands under the fenced figures directory and the anchor embeds it with the project-absolute src.
